title_en: Yaoxian Cement Plant v. China Building Materials Group Corporation and Shaanxi Building Materials General Company — dispute over conversion of creditor's rights into capital contribution
ruling_gist_en: The conversion of central-level 'appropriation-to-loan', 'special appropriation-to-loan', and 'basic construction operational funds' into state capital contributions to enterprises is carried out in accordance with the respective implementation measures of the former State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance, through a process of application by the fund-using units and approval by the former State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance. This process does not reflect the will of the unit acting as the state capital contributor or the unit receiving the capital, and is different from the conversion of creditor's rights into capital contributions that occurs between ordinary creditors and debtors. Its nature is that of a policy-based conversion of creditor's rights into capital contributions. Therefore, whether the aforesaid debts can be converted into state capital contributions, which unit acts as the state capital contributor, and to which unit the capital is contributed, are all matters within the scope of administrative functions exercised by the relevant state administrative authorities, and do not fall within the scope of civil litigation accepted by the people's courts. Disputes arising between parties over the above issues shall be resolved through coordination by the relevant administrative authorities; if there is any objection to the specific administrative acts of the relevant administrative authorities in coordination and resolution, relief may be sought in accordance with the relevant provisions of administrative law.

full_text_en:
Yao County Cement Plant v. China Building Materials Group Corporation,
Shaanxi Provincial Building Materials General Company
— dispute over conversion of creditor's rights into capital contributions

Ruling Summary

The conversion of central-level "appropriation-turned-loans", "special appropriation-turned-loans", and "infrastructure operating funds" into state capital contributions to enterprises is carried out respectively in accordance with the relevant implementing measures of the former State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance, through the application of the fund-using entity and the approval of the former State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance. Such conversion does not reflect the will of the entity performing the functions of state capital contributor or the will of the funded entity, and differs from the conversion of ordinary creditor-debtor relationships into capital contributions. Its nature is that of a policy-based conversion of creditor's rights into capital contributions. Therefore, issues such as whether the aforesaid debts can be converted into state capital contributions, which entity shall perform the functions of state capital contributor on behalf of the state, and to which entity the contributions shall be made, all fall within the scope of administrative authority exercised by the relevant state administrative authorities, and do not fall within the scope of civil cases accepted by the People's Courts. Disputes arising between the parties over the above issues shall be resolved through coordination by the relevant administrative authorities; if a party challenges the specific administrative act of such coordination or resolution, it may seek relief in accordance with the relevant provisions of administrative law.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2005) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 203

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Shaanxi Province Yao County Cement Plant, domiciled at: East Suburb, Yaozhou District, Tongchuan City, Shaanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Lan Jianwen, Factory Manager of the Plant.
Agents ad litem: Cao Jianbin, an employee of the Plant.
Chen Yaoquan, an attorney of Beijing Tiantong Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Building Materials Group Corporation, domiciled at: No. 2 Zizhuyuan South Road, Haidian District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Song Zhiping, General Manager of the Corporation.
Agents ad litem: Huang Min, an employee of China Building Materials Asset Management Company.
Zhang Mingpeng, an attorney of Beijing Youbang Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Shaanxi Provincial Building Materials General Company, domiciled at: No. 162 Xiqi Road, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.
Legal Representative: Guo Hanwen, General Manager of the Company.

The appellant, Shaanxi Province Yao County Cement Plant (hereinafter referred to as Yao County Cement Plant), filed an appeal with this Court against the civil judgment (2004) Shan Min Er Chu Zi No. 7 rendered by the Shaanxi High People's Court in the case of dispute over conversion of creditor's rights into capital contributions brought by the appellee, China Building Materials Group Corporation (renamed from China New Building Materials (Group) Corporation, hereinafter uniformly referred to as the Group Corporation), and the defendant at first instance, Shaanxi Provincial Building Materials General Company (hereinafter referred to as the Building Materials General Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, composed of presiding judge Wu Qingbao, acting judges Gong Bangyou and Liu Min, with court clerk Zhao Suijun, to hear the case. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found that: From 1985 to 1998, Yao County Cement Plant, for the expansion of its No. 5 Kiln project, successively used national central-level "appropriation-turned-loan" funds of RMB 8.25 million, "special appropriation-turned-loan" funds of RMB 25 million, and "infrastructure operating funds" of RMB 14 million. Yao County Cement Plant failed to repay these three sums of funds.

In December 1996, the State Development Planning Commission (hereinafter referred to as the State Planning Commission) and the Ministry of Finance formulated and issued the "Implementing Measures for Converting the Principal and Interest Balance of Central-Level 'Appropriation-Turned-Loan' Funds into State Capital". Pursuant thereto, on January 21, 1997, Yao County Cement Plant submitted, by way of its document Shan Yao Ni Zheng Fa (1997) No. 006 titled "Request of Yao County Cement Plant for Converting the Principal and Interest Balance of Central-Level 'Appropriation-Turned-Loan' Funds into State Capital", to the Finance and State-owned Assets Supervision Department of the State Building Materials Industry Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the State Building Materials Bureau), an application to convert the principal and interest of the central-level "appropriation-turned-loan" funds of RMB 8.25 million and the "special appropriation-turned-loan" funds of RMB 25 million used by it into state capital. In the same year, the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance, by document Ji Tou Zi (1997) No. 2586, converted the principal and interest balance of the central-level "appropriation-turned-loan" funds of the State Building Materials Bureau into state capital, tentatively designating the State Building Materials Bureau as the capital contributor. The application for converting the "special appropriation-turned-loan" funds into state capital was not approved because there was then no policy basis for doing so. On October 7, 1999, in accordance with the central government's policy on the delinking of enterprises, and based on the Group Corporation's "Application for Converting Part of the Principal and Interest Balance of Central-Level 'Appropriation-Turned-Loan' Funds of the State Building Materials Bureau into State Capital and Authorizing the Group Corporation to Manage the Same" and the State Building Materials Bureau's "Letter on Applying for Authorization to the Group Corporation to Manage Part of the Principal and Interest Balance of Central-Level 'Appropriation-Turned-Loan' Funds Converted into State Capital", the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance, by document Ji Tou Zi (1999) No. 1999, approved the Group Corporation as the capital contributor for the conversion of central-level "appropriation-turned-loan" funds (including the "appropriation-turned-loan" funds of RMB 8.25 million for Yao County Cement Plant and interest of RMB 2,322,300.83) into state capital in some building materials enterprises.

In May 1998, the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance formulated and issued the "Implementing Measures for Converting the Principal and Interest Balance of Central-Level Infrastructure Operating Funds into State Capital". On April 21, 2000, the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance, by document Ji Tou Zi (2000) No. 444, approved the conversion of central-level infrastructure operating fund entrusted loans used by 25 enterprises into state capital of the Group Corporation, authorizing the Corporation to perform the functions of capital contributor, including the principal of RMB 14 million and interest of RMB 2,817,427.34 owed by Yao County Cement Plant.

In December 1999, the Ministry of Finance formulated and issued the "Implementing Measures for Converting the Principal and Interest Balance of Central-Level 'Special Appropriation-Turned-Loan' Funds into State Capital". On January 14, 2000, Shaanxi Qinda Cement Plant (hereinafter referred to as Qinda Cement Plant), by its document Shan Qin Shui Zheng Fa (2000) No. 001 titled "Request of Qinda Cement Plant for Converting the Principal and Interest Balance of Central-Level 'Special Appropriation-Turned-Loan' Funds into State Capital", applied to the Enterprise Reform Department of the State Building Materials Bureau to convert the principal and interest of the central-level "special appropriation-turned-loan" funds of RMB 25 million borrowed by its predecessor, the No. 5 Kiln Expansion Office of Yao County Cement Plant (hereinafter referred to as the No. 5 Kiln Expansion Office), into state capital. On April 3 of the same year, the Ministry of Finance, by letter Cai Ji Zi (2000) No. 64, replied to the State Building Materials Bureau and the Group Corporation, approving the conversion of the principal and interest of the "special appropriation-turned-loan" funds of 18 enterprises formerly under the State Building Materials Bureau into state capital of the Group Corporation, authorizing the Corporation to perform the functions of capital contributor. The appendix to the letter, a table of the principal and interest balance of central-level "special appropriation-turned-loan" funds of the Group Corporation, noted: "Qinda Cement Plant (Yao County Cement Plant): principal RMB 25 million, interest RMB 8,265,631.70."

It was further found that: All loans of the three sums of funds involved in this case were used for the expansion project of Yao County Cement Plant — the No. 5 Kiln project. The No. 5 Kiln project was completed at the end of 1993, and the No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant (not an enterprise legal person, hereinafter referred to as the No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant) was established on that basis. On June 1, 1998, the Building Materials General Company, by its document Shan Jian Cai Zong Zi Fa (1998) No. 116 titled "Request of the Building Materials General Company for Defining Property Rights of State-owned Assets of Qinda Cement Plant and Verifying State Capital", applied to the Shaanxi Provincial State-owned Assets Administration Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Shaanxi State-owned Assets Bureau) to define the property rights of state-owned assets invested in Qinda Cement Plant (established by spinning off the No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant) and to verify the state capital. The Shaanxi State-owned Assets Bureau approved the spin-off of the No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant and the establishment of Qinda Cement Plant. On March 20, 2003, Qinda Cement Plant submitted to its superior, the Building Materials General Company, its document Qin Da Zheng Fa (2003) No. 002 titled "Report on the Conversion of 'Appropriation-Turned-Loans', 'Special Appropriation-Turned-Loans', and 'Operating Funds' into Additional State Capital", stating that the plant had successively added state capital of RMB 60.66 million (i.e., the three sums of funds involved in this case), with the capital contributor being the Group Corporation. Based on this, the Building Materials General Company applied to the Shaanxi Provincial Department of Finance to convert the central-level "appropriation-turned-loans", central-level "special appropriation-turned-loans", and central-level "infrastructure operating funds" used by Yao County Cement Plant when constructing the No. 5 Kiln production line, totaling RMB 60,651,359.24 (principal of RMB 47,250,000 and interest of RMB 13,401,359.24), into state capital of Qinda Cement Plant, with the Group Corporation performing the functions of capital contributor. The Shaanxi Provincial Department of Finance, by its document Shan Cai Ban Qi (2003) No. 86 titled "Notice on Converting Central-Level 'Appropriation-Turned-Loans', 'Special Appropriation-Turned-Loans', and 'Operating Funds' of Qinda Cement Plant into State Capital", approved the application of the Building Materials General Company.

On April 21, 2004, the Group Corporation filed a lawsuit with the Shaanxi High People's Court on the ground that Yao County Cement Plant and the Building Materials General Company had failed to register the corresponding changes in accordance with the approvals of the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance (Ji Tou Zi [1999] No. 1999, Ji Tou Zi [2000] No. 444, and Cai Ji Zi [2000] No. 64) which agreed that the Group Corporation would be the capital contributor for the conversion of the three sums of funds involved into state capital. The Group Corporation requested the court to: confirm that the Group Corporation was the capital contributor of Yao County Cement Plant, with a capital contribution amount of RMB 60,651,359.24; order Yao County Cement Plant and the Building Materials General Company to complete the relevant registration procedures; and require Yao County Cement Plant and the Group Corporation to bear the case acceptance fee.

After trial, the court of first instance held that the focus of the dispute between the parties was whether the Group Corporation should be the capital contributor of Yao County Cement Plant, and the key to this was whether Yao County Cement Plant was the debtor of the three sums of funds involved in this case. Although Yao County Cement Plant and the Building Materials General Company argued that the borrower of the three sums of funds was the predecessor of Qinda Cement Plant, the No. 5 Kiln Expansion Office, not Yao County Cement Plant, and that the three sums of funds borrowed were also used for the construction of the No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant, and that the No. 5 Kiln Expansion Office, the No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant, and Yao County Cement Plant were each independent, therefore the debtor of the three sums of funds should be Qinda Cement Plant. However, the appendices to the documents of the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance regarding the conversion of the three sums of funds into state capital, with the Group Corporation performing the functions of capital contributor, provided by the Group Corporation, indicated that the debtor of the three sums of funds involved was Yao County Cement Plant. Since the three sums of funds borrowed in the name of the No. 5 Kiln Expansion Office were all used for the expansion project of Yao County Cement Plant — the No. 5 Kiln project, and the No. 5 Kiln Expansion Office and the No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant had not undergone industrial and commercial registration, they did not enjoy independent civil subject status according to law and were merely internal organs of Yao County Cement Plant. It was clear that the three sums of funds were borrowed by Yao County Cement Plant. Furthermore, the act of Yao County Cement Plant applying to convert the three sums of funds involved into state capital also indicated that Yao County Cement Plant had expressly recognized its position as debtor. Therefore, Yao County Cement Plant should be the debtor of the three sums of funds involved. The argument of the two defendants that Yao County Cement Plant was not the debtor of the three sums of funds could not be sustained.

As for the issue that the document of the Shaanxi Provincial Department of Finance confirmed the Group Corporation as the capital contributor of Qinda Cement Plant, since the three sums of funds involved were central-level funds and belonged to central financial claims, the local government had no authority to dispose of them. Moreover, the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance had already issued documents on the conversion of these three sums of funds into state capital, authorizing the Group Corporation to perform the functions of capital contributor on behalf of the state for the capital contribution to Yao County Cement Plant. Therefore, the relevant confirmation document of the Shaanxi Provincial Department of Finance provided by the defendants could not be used as a basis for confirming the enterprise to which the Group Corporation was the capital contributor.

In summary, the Group Corporation's claim for confirmation as the capital contributor of Yao County Cement Plant, based on the relevant documents of the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance, had sufficient factual basis and was also in line with national policies and laws. The court accepted this. The Group Corporation claimed a capital contribution amount of RMB 60,651,359.24, to which the opposing parties did not object, and the court also confirmed this. As the superior supervisory unit of Yao County Cement Plant, the Building Materials General Company should, together with Yao County Cement Plant, handle the registration procedures for the Group Corporation as the capital contributor of Yao County Cement Plant within a reasonable period. In accordance with Article 84 and Article 106(1) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, and Article 14(2) of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Dispute Cases Related to Enterprise Restructuring, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. Confirmed that the Group Corporation was the capital contributor of Yao County Cement Plant, with a capital contribution amount of RMB 60,651,359.24; 2. Yao County Cement Plant and the Building Materials General Company shall complete the registration procedures for the Group Corporation as the capital contributor of Yao County Cement Plant within 30 days after this judgment takes effect. The case acceptance fee of RMB 313,266 was to be borne equally by Yao County Cement Plant and the Building Materials General Company.

Yao County Cement Plant, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Shaanxi High People's Court, appealed to this Court, arguing: The borrowers of the three sums of funds involved in this case were all the predecessor of Qinda Cement Plant, the No. 5 Kiln Expansion Office. The No. 5 Kiln Expansion Office was completely independent from Yao County Cement Plant in terms of project approval, actual construction, and operation. After the project was completed, the established No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant was a factual independent civil subject with independent property and paid-in capital, and was responsible for its own profits and losses, paid taxes independently, and could be declared bankrupt according to the Bankruptcy Law when its assets were insufficient to cover its debts. The State Building Materials Bureau recognized that Qinda Cement Plant was renamed from the No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant, and the creditor of the three sums of funds, the Yaoxian Branch of China Construction Bank, also recognized Qinda Cement Plant as the debtor. The State Building Materials Bureau and the Ministry of Finance approved Qinda Cement Plant's application to convert the additional state capital, and the state had directly designated the RMB 25 million "special appropriation-turned-loan" funds as Qinda Cement Plant's state capital. The converted state capital was also registered as state-owned assets held by Qinda Cement Plant. Qinda Cement Plant should be the funded entity after the conversion of the three sums of funds into state capital. The first instance judgment erroneously determined that the No. 5 Kiln Expansion Office and the No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant were internal organs of Yao County Cement Plant, and confirmed Yao County Cement Plant as the funded entity. In particular, the RMB 25 million "special appropriation-turned-loan" funds were applied for by Qinda Cement Plant to be converted into its own state capital, and the state had already approved their conversion into Qinda Cement Plant's state capital. The Group Corporation's claim and the outcome of the case had a legal interest in Qinda Cement Plant, and Qinda Cement Plant should have been notified by law to participate in the proceedings as a third party. The court of first instance failed to notify Qinda Cement Plant to participate in the proceedings, resulting in the state capital legally registered by Qinda Cement Plant being turned into state capital of Yao County Cement Plant through the court's judgment, negating the funded entity determined by the Ministry of Finance in accordance with national policy, and rendering Qinda Cement Plant's legitimate rights and interests in suspense. The first instance judgment had unclear findings of fact and violated statutory procedures. Yao County Cement Plant requested the court to revoke the first instance judgment, dismiss the Group Corporation's claim, and order the Group Corporation to bear the case acceptance fee.

The appellee, the Group Corporation, argued in its response: 1. The original debtor of the three sums of funds involved in this case should be Yao County Cement Plant. The No. 5 Kiln Expansion Office and the No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant were both independent legal persons but internal organs of Yao County Cement Plant. Yao County Cement Plant did not raise any objection to the loan contracts signed by its internal organs and also accepted the performance of the contracts by the other party. Therefore, the rights and obligations under the contracts should be borne by Yao County Cement Plant. Qinda Cement Plant was a brand-new civil subject with no legal relationship with the No. 5 Kiln Expansion Office or the No. 5 Kiln Branch Plant. There was no inherent "development and evolution" relationship between Qinda Cement Plant and Yao County Cement Plant, and thus no succession of rights and obligations between the two legal entity subjects. 2. As for the fact of converting Yao County Cement Plant's debts into state capital, the Ministry of Finance and the State Planning Commission had made clear approvals in documents Ji Tou Zi [1999] No. 1999, Cai Ji Zi [2000] No. 64, and Ji Tou Zi [2000] No. 444. Yao County Cement Plant's arguments on appeal, such as that the above three documents of the Ministry of Finance and the State Planning Commission were erroneous in disposing of state-owned assets, or that decisions of local administrative organs in Shaanxi Province could override decisions of the central Ministry of Finance and the State Planning Commission, or that Shaanxi provincial state-owned assets management institutions could dispose of central-level state-owned assets, were all wrong. The basic principle of state-owned assets management in China is hierarchical management: central-level state-owned assets are managed by the central government, and local governments only manage local state-owned assets. The creditor's rights at issue in this case were central-level state-owned assets. The above three documents of the Ministry of Finance and the State Planning Commission should be deemed valid evidence. In contrast, Document Shan Cai Ban Qi [2003] No. 86 of the Shaanxi Provincial Department of Finance, which disposed of central-level state-owned assets, was a clear act of exceeding authority and should not be admitted. 3. Although Document Cai Ji Zi [2000] No. 64 indicated that the project using the funds was "Qinda Cement Plant (Yao County Cement Plant)", it should still be determined that Yao County Cement Plant was the funded entity after the conversion of that sum of funds into state capital. Yao County Cement Plant was the actual user of the three sums of funds. Although the three sums of funds had different names, they were inseparable in nature. According to the documents of the Ministry of Finance and the State Planning Commission, the method of converting the three types of funds into state capital was the same and also inseparable. On January 14, 2000, although Qinda Cement Plant applied in its own name to the State Building Materials Bureau to convert the special appropriation-turned-loan funds into its own state capital, the Ministry of Finance's document stated it as "Qinda Cement Plant (Yao County Cement Plant)", which was distinctly different from Qinda Cement Plant's request. Yao County Cement Plant had previously applied in its own name to the state in 1997 to convert this sum of funds into state capital, indicating that it recognized itself as the debtor of that sum of funds. The superior unit of Yao County Cement Plant, the Building Materials General Company, also acknowledged that the user of the three sums of funds was Yao County Cement Plant, not Qinda Cement Plant. Therefore, the Group Corporation requested that the appeal be dismissed and the first instance judgment be affirmed.

During the second instance, the defendant at first instance, the Building Materials General Company, submitted a written explanation to this Court stating that, in accordance with Document Shan Guo Qi Gai Ban Fa [2005] No. 006 "Notice on Issues Related to the Transfer of Some Provincial State-owned Enterprises under the Management of Tongchuan and Other Four Cities and One District", the Building Materials General Company had completed the handover procedures for the transfer of Yao County Cement Plant to the Tongchuan Municipal Party Committee and Government on November 4, 2005, and that it had lost the qualification to appear in court for the proceedings. It requested that relevant matters be coordinated with the Tongchuan Municipal State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission.

After hearing the case, this Court is of the opinion that the Group Corporation's claim in this case is for confirmation that it is the capital contributor of Yao County Cement Plant and for an order that Yao County Cement Plant and the Building Materials General Company complete the corresponding registration procedures, rather than for a request that Yao County Cement Plant repay the three sums of debts involved. Therefore, the focus of the dispute in this case is whether the Group Corporation is the capital contributor of Yao County Cement Plant, not a dispute over creditor's rights and debts. Whether Yao County Cement Plant is the debtor of the three sums of funds involved is not within the scope of trial of this case. The court of first instance treated the issue of whether Yao County Cement Plant was the debtor of the three loan sums involved in this case as the key to the trial, and, on the premise of confirming Yao County Cement Plant as the debtor of the three loans, improperly determined the Group Corporation as the capital contributor of Yao County Cement Plant.

The three debts in this case were converted into state capital contributions to the enterprise pursuant to the respective implementation measures of the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance concerning the conversion of the principal and interest balances of central-level "appropriation-to-loan" funds, "special appropriation-to-loan" funds, and "infrastructure operational" funds into state capital. This conversion was effected through application by the borrowing unit and approval by the State Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance. It did not reflect the will of the group company, which performs the function of the state capital contributor, or the will of the funded enterprises, Yaoxian Cement Plant or Qinda Cement Plant. Unlike the conversion of debts into equity between ordinary creditors and debtors, this conversion is, by its nature, a policy-based conversion of debts into equity. Therefore, issues such as whether an enterprise's debts may be converted into state capital contributions to it, which entity specifically performs the function of the state capital contributor, and which enterprise the contributions are ultimately converted into, are all matters falling within the scope of the exercise of administrative powers by the relevant state administrative authorities, not within the scope of civil litigation accepted by the people's courts. Consequently, the disputes arising during the process of converting the three debts into state capital should be resolved through coordination by the relevant administrative authorities. If there are objections to the specific administrative actions of the relevant administrative authorities, recourse may be sought in accordance with the relevant provisions of administrative law. As the claims filed by the group company in this case do not fall within the scope of civil litigation accepted by the people's courts, the court of first instance erred in accepting the case as a civil action, and this court hereby corrects this in accordance with the law. Pursuant to Article 108, Paragraph 1(3) of Article 140, and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, as well as Article 186 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court rules as follows:

1. Reverse the Civil Judgment (2004) Shan Min Er Chu Zi No. 7 of the Shaanxi High People's Court;

2. Dismiss the lawsuit filed by China National Building Materials Group Corporation.

The court acceptance fees for the first and second instances shall each be RMB 313,266, both borne by China National Building Materials Group Corporation.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Wu Qingbao

Acting Judge: Gong Bangyou

Acting Judge: Liu Min

May 15, 2006

Clerk: Zhao Suijun
